conventions.convention: The classical field is a smooth real two-form on a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature (−,+,+,+). Closed means dF=0; a global potential means F=dA for a global smooth real one-form.

The optional sector fixes a right principal U(1) bundle P and an independent normalization κ₀>0 in webers. Aᵢ=κ₀aᵢ and F=κ₀daᵢ locally; this is additional model data rather than a quantum charge rule.
When gᵢⱼ=exp(ifᵢⱼ), the overlap rule is aⱼ=aᵢ+dfᵢⱼ and the fibre-angle rule is θⱼ=θᵢ−fᵢⱼ. Horizontal transport obeys θ̇=−a(γ̇), giving holonomy exp(−i∫γ a).
Spatial spheres have outward orientation. The north-to-south transition is exp(−2ibφ/κ₀), so its winding is −2b/κ₀ while the normalized outward flux is +2b/κ₀.
The global circle angular form is ν=−iw⁻¹dw; dφ denotes its expression on an angle chart, without assuming a global real-valued angle. Its positive-circle period is 2π.

load_bearing.statement: A classical electromagnetic field is a smooth real two-form F. Closedness is dF=0; a potential on U satisfies dA_U=F|_U. An optional circle-normalized connection sector fixes the bundle P and normalization κ₀, with Aᵢ=κ₀aᵢ and F|Uᵢ=κ₀daᵢ.

Under the smooth homogeneous Maxwell law, local potentials exist on star-shaped coordinate domains. On punctured Minkowski spacetime, F_b=b sinθ dθ∧dφ has outward sphere flux 4πb and no global potential for b≠0. Its stated north/south potentials patch with normalization κ₀ exactly when 2b/κ₀∈ℤ. The separate flat connection κ₀aν has holonomy exp(−2πia) and is gauge trivial exactly when a∈ℤ.
